title: THE D.B. COOPER MYSTERY | Part 3: The Money in the Sand
description:
For nine years, not a single ransom bill turned up. Then, in 1980, an eight-year-old boy digging on a riverbank found something that made the mystery even stranger.

Part 3 of an animated true-crime series about the D.B. Cooper case.

#dbcooper #truecrime #unsolvedmystery #animation #mystery

series.name: The D.B. Cooper Mystery
series.previously: At eight thirteen p.m., somewhere over southwest Washington, Dan Cooper jumped from Flight three-oh-five into a freezing storm, with two hundred thousand dollars. When the jet landed in Reno, he was gone.

shots.say: By the next morning, the story was on every front page in America.
Early on, police questioned a Portland man whose name really was D. B. Cooper. He was cleared almost immediately. But a reporter repeated the name, and it stuck forever.
shots.caption: "D.B. COOPER"

shots.say: Using the flight path and the timing of that bump, the FBI estimated where he might have landed. Thick forest, north of Portland, near the Lewis River.
Hundreds of agents and soldiers searched those woods. On foot. From helicopters. Even with boats on the lakes.
They found nothing. No parachute. No body. No money.
shots.caption: NOTHING.

shots.say: Banks across the country were given the list of serial numbers. If even one of those bills was ever spent, the FBI would know.
Months passed. Then years. Not a single bill ever turned up.
shots.caption: NOT ONE BILL.

shots.say: An eight-year-old boy was on a family trip along the Columbia River, at a sandy beach called Tena Bar. He was raking the sand flat to build a campfire.
Just under the surface, he found three bundles of old twenty-dollar bills. Wet. Rotting. Still held together with rubber bands.
The FBI checked the serial numbers. They matched. It was Cooper's money. About five thousand eight hundred dollars.
shots.caption: IT MATCHED.

shots.say: Nine years of silence. And then, a pile of the ransom, sitting in the sand.
But the discovery made the mystery stranger, not simpler. Tena Bar is about twenty miles from where the FBI believed he landed.
Did the money wash down a creek into the river? Was it buried there by someone? Did Cooper drop it as he fled? Experts have argued about it for decades.
The rest of the money, more than one hundred ninety thousand dollars, has never been found.
shots.caption: $194,200 MISSING.

shots.say: Which left investigators with one real clue. The black clip-on tie he left behind on his seat.
shots.caption: THE TIE.
